\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{తేనెటీగ} (tēneṭīga)}{తేనెటీగ (tēneṭīga)}]{\te{తేనెటీగ} (tēneṭīga) — a bee}

\label{lesson:TE-C187-tenetiga}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for twins, then the Telugu for a baby.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{తేనెటీగ}}
\textbf{\te{తేనెటీగ}} — \emph{tēneṭīga} — \textquotedblleft{}a bee\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{తేనెటీగ}} (\emph{tēneṭīga}) is native Dravidian: \emph{tēne}, \textquotedblleft{}honey\textquotedblright{}, one word with Tamil \emph{tēṉ} (DEDR 3268), and \emph{īga}, \textquotedblleft{}fly\textquotedblright{}, one word with Tamil \emph{ī}, \textquotedblleft{}fly, bee\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 533). For the first, DEDR compares, with a query, Prakrit \emph{tiṇisa}, \textquotedblleft{}honeycomb\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tēneṭīga}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tēneṭīga}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{tēneṭīga}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for twins, then the Telugu for a baby, then say \emph{tēneṭīga} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{బల్లి} (balli)}{బల్లి (balli)}]{\te{బల్లి} (balli) — a lizard, a gecko}

\label{lesson:TE-C187-balli}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a baby, then the Telugu for a bee.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{బల్లి}}
\textbf{\te{బల్లి}} — \emph{balli} — \textquotedblleft{}a lizard, a gecko\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{బల్లి}} (\emph{balli}) is native Dravidian. DEDR 3994 lists \emph{palli} and \emph{balli}, \textquotedblleft{}lizard\textquotedblright{}, with Tamil \emph{palli} and Kannada \emph{palli}. DEDR compares Sanskrit \emph{pallī}, \textquotedblleft{}small house lizard\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 7973), a lexicon word.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{పురుగు} (purugu)}{పురుగు (purugu)}]{\te{పురుగు} (purugu) — an insect, a worm}

\label{lesson:TE-C187-purugu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a bee, then the Telugu for a lizard.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{పురుగు}}
\textbf{\te{పురుగు}} — \emph{purugu} — \textquotedblleft{}an insect, a worm\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{పురుగు}} (\emph{purugu}) is native Dravidian. DEDR 4312 lists \emph{purugu}, \textquotedblleft{}worm, any insect\textquotedblright{}, with Tamil \emph{puḻu}, \textquotedblleft{}worm\textquotedblright{}, and Kannada \emph{puḻu}, \textquotedblleft{}worm, insect\textquotedblright{}. DEDR compares several Sanskrit words for \textquotedblleft{}worm\textquotedblright{}, among them \emph{pīlu}, \textquotedblleft{}worm\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8240), which CDIAL takes from Dravidian.
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}
